payload.title: The finding-id space is exhausted for domain ARIA: the sequence is three digits, spelled by hand at every writer and reader, so finding-registry add refuses at 999 and no one site can be widened alone
evidence: tools/gates/finding-registry-store.ts:472-475 (nextFindingId: `if (next > 999) throw RangeError('Finding ID space exhausted for domain ... (maximum 999)')`, padStart(3))
tools/gates/finding-registry.ts:235-237 (reservation ledger: `reservation.sequence > 999` and a three-digit suffix check)
tools/gates/finding-registry.ts:293-294 (reserveFindingId reads the sequence as `findingId.slice(-3)` and refuses above 999)
tools/gates/finding-registry-store.spec.ts:136 (the exhaustion case pins INFRA-LOW-999 as the last id)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md one owner per concept and the architectural-solution hierarchy tiers 1 and 3: the grammar of a finding id has one owner per language, and a second spelling of it is detected at build time
payload.notes: Found 2026-10-25 by the D6-SEC clerk: `finding-registry add` refuses with 'Finding ID space exhausted for domain ARIA (maximum 999)' once ARIA ids 974-999 are claimed (registry rows, sibling worktree registries and the reservation ledger), so any package that registers a finding in that domain fails. Widening the constant in the allocator alone leaves the ledger, the explicit-append shape, the orphan heading, the Closes trailer grammar, the row schema and the kernel readers refusing the ids the allocator issues. Close condition: one TypeScript owner (tools/gates/finding-id-grammar.ts) and one Python owner (aria_kernel/finding_id_grammar.py) of the grammar, held to one table (tools/gates/fixtures/finding-id-grammar-table.json); ids 001..999 stay valid and are never rewritten, 1000..9999 are allocatable; every restatement under tools/, tests/ and aria-kernel/ is gone and tests/invariants/finding-id-grammar.spec.ts fails a new one. Out of scope: renumbering or aliasing existing ids, F-NNN ids, a second domain.
